rce.downloads-and-pipes-straight-into-a-.what: It downloads a program from the internet and runs it immediately, without anyone checking it first.
rce.downloads-and-pipes-straight-into-a-.like: eating food a stranger hands you without looking at it.
rce.downloads-and-pipes-straight-into-a-.fix: Delete it and rebuild from the skill's purpose; never patch.

rce.decodes-hidden-payload-into-a-shell.what: It unscrambles hidden code and runs it right away, a classic way to hide malware.
rce.decodes-hidden-payload-into-a-shell.like: a sealed envelope that tells your computer what to do.
rce.decodes-hidden-payload-into-a-shell.fix: Delete it and rebuild from the skill's purpose; never patch.

rce.encoded-powershell-payload.what: It runs a scrambled Windows command that nobody can read before it runs.
rce.encoded-powershell-payload.like: signing a contract written in a code you can't read.
rce.encoded-powershell-payload.fix: Delete it and rebuild from the skill's purpose; never patch.

rce.dynamic-code-execution.what: The code builds commands as text and runs them, so it could run something unexpected.
rce.dynamic-code-execution.like: following instructions that get written while you walk.
rce.dynamic-code-execution.fix: Replace with a fixed command list or a safe parser.

rce.dynamic-js-code-execution.what: JavaScript code is created from text and run on the fly, so its behavior can't be checked in advance.
rce.dynamic-js-code-execution.like: a recipe that rewrites itself while you cook.

rce.dynamic-import-compile.what: The code loads or builds other code while running, which can hide what it really does.
rce.dynamic-import-compile.like: a toolbox that grabs unknown tools mid-job.
rce.dynamic-import-compile.fix: Import fixed modules by name at the top.

rce.runs-shell-commands.what: It runs commands on your computer. Often normal, but the exact commands matter.
rce.runs-shell-commands.like: a helper using your keyboard; fine if you see what they type.
rce.runs-shell-commands.fix: Keep only fixed, listed commands with no user text inside.

rce.runs-a-package-fetched-at-runtime.what: It downloads and runs a package from the internet each time, and the author can change it later.
rce.runs-a-package-fetched-at-runtime.like: a delivery that could contain something different each day.
rce.runs-a-package-fetched-at-runtime.fix: Pin the package to one exact version.

deps.installs-dependencies.what: It installs extra software, which could be outdated, mistyped or tampered with.
deps.installs-dependencies.like: borrowing parts from strangers to build your gadget.
deps.installs-dependencies.fix: Pin every dependency to an exact version and check the names.

deps.npm-install-time-script.what: A script runs automatically the moment this package is installed, before you can look at it.
deps.npm-install-time-script.like: a package that opens itself when it arrives.

secrets.touches-ssh-keys.what: It touches your SSH keys, the files that prove who you are to servers and GitHub.
secrets.touches-ssh-keys.like: copying the master key to your house.
secrets.touches-ssh-keys.fix: Remove the SSH access; it is not needed for a skill.

secrets.touches-cloud-dev-credentials.what: It reads saved logins for cloud or developer tools like AWS, npm or git.
secrets.touches-cloud-dev-credentials.like: reading the sticky note where you wrote your passwords.
secrets.touches-cloud-dev-credentials.fix: Remove the credential read; ask for only the one value needed.

secrets.touches-claude-credentials-confi.what: It reads Claude's login or settings files, which could let someone use your account.
secrets.touches-claude-credentials-confi.fix: Remove the read of Claude credentials and config.

secrets.reads-macos-keychain.what: It reads the Mac Keychain, where your saved passwords live.

secrets.reads-browser-password-manager-s.what: It reads browser or password-manager data: saved logins, cookies or vault files.
secrets.reads-browser-password-manager-s.like: rummaging through your wallet for cards and keys.
secrets.reads-browser-password-manager-s.fix: Remove access to browser and password-manager data.

secrets.dumps-all-environment-variables.what: It collects every hidden setting on your computer, which often include passwords and keys.
secrets.dumps-all-environment-variables.like: photographing every key on your keyring.
secrets.dumps-all-environment-variables.fix: Read only the one named setting it truly needs.

secrets.mentions-secrets-tokens.what: The code mentions keys, tokens or passwords. It may be harmless, but how it uses them matters.
secrets.mentions-secrets-tokens.like: a note saying 'bring the keys'; fine if they stay home.
secrets.mentions-secrets-tokens.fix: Check use; pass only the one needed value in explicitly.

secrets.reads-env-files.what: .env files hold project passwords and keys, and this reads them.
secrets.reads-env-files.like: peeking into a drawer of spare keys.
secrets.reads-env-files.fix: Stop reading .env; ask the user for the one value needed.

privacy.reads-personal-data.what: It reads personal data like messages, contacts, mail or command history.
privacy.reads-personal-data.fix: Remove the personal-data read; work only on files you name.

privacy.screen-clipboard-keyboard-captur.what: It can capture your screen, clipboard or keystrokes, which may include private things.
privacy.screen-clipboard-keyboard-captur.fix: Remove the capture; use only what you give it.

exfil.posts-to-chat-webhook.what: It sends data to a chat webhook (Discord, Slack, Telegram), a favorite way to steal data quietly.
exfil.posts-to-chat-webhook.like: mailing your files to a stranger's PO box.
exfil.posts-to-chat-webhook.fix: Delete the webhook call; rebuild without outbound data.

exfil.known-exfil-tunnel-paste-endpoint.what: It talks to a site known for catching stolen data or tunneling into computers.
exfil.known-exfil-tunnel-paste-endpoint.like: a courier who only works for thieves.
exfil.known-exfil-tunnel-paste-endpoint.fix: Delete the call; rebuild without outbound data.

exfil.raw-network-socket-reverse-shell-p.what: It opens a raw network connection, the pattern attackers use to control a computer remotely.
exfil.raw-network-socket-reverse-shell-p.like: leaving a back door open for a stranger.

exfil.sends-data-over-http.what: It sends data over the internet. Fine for a stated purpose, bad if it ships your data.
exfil.sends-data-over-http.like: posting a letter; harmless unless it holds your secrets.
exfil.sends-data-over-http.fix: Limit it to one documented domain that gets no user data.

exfil.telemetry-analytics.what: It reports how you use it to an analytics service.
exfil.telemetry-analytics.like: a shop counting visitors and watching what they do.

backdoor.installs-persistence.what: It makes itself run again every time your computer starts or you log in.
backdoor.installs-persistence.like: moving into your house and refusing to leave.
backdoor.installs-persistence.fix: Delete the startup step; run only when invoked.

backdoor.edits-shell-startup-files.what: It changes files that run each time you open a terminal, so it can come back unseen.
backdoor.edits-shell-startup-files.like: adding a hidden step to your morning routine.
backdoor.edits-shell-startup-files.fix: Remove the edit; tell the user what to add.

backdoor.privilege-escalation.what: It asks for administrator power over your computer.

backdoor.bypasses-macos-security.what: It tries to switch off Mac protections like Gatekeeper, permission prompts or quarantine.

claude-tamper.disables-claude-permission.what: It turns off Claude's safety questions, so it can act without asking you.
claude-tamper.disables-claude-permission.like: cutting the brakes on a car.
claude-tamper.disables-claude-permission.fix: Delete it; rebuild without changing Claude's permission settings.

claude-tamper.adds-edits-claude-hooks-or.what: It changes Claude's settings or hooks, so it can run things automatically later.
claude-tamper.adds-edits-claude-hooks-or.fix: Remove the edits; tell the user what to change.

claude-tamper.grants-itself-tool-permiss.what: It gives itself permission to use tools without asking you.

claude-tamper.writes-to-claude-memory-sk.what: It writes into Claude's memory, rules or other skills, which can change how Claude behaves.
claude-tamper.writes-to-claude-memory-sk.like: adding notes to your assistant's handbook.
claude-tamper.writes-to-claude-memory-sk.fix: Remove the writes; tell the user what to change.

claude-tamper.registers-mcp-servers.what: It connects Claude to extra tool servers that can read data or take actions.
claude-tamper.registers-mcp-servers.like: plugging in a device you haven't inspected.
claude-tamper.registers-mcp-servers.fix: Remove registration, or list each server and what it can do.

injection.instruction-override-attempt.what: The text tries to make Claude ignore its earlier rules or yours.
injection.instruction-override-attempt.fix: Delete the override text; keep plain task steps.

injection.hides-actions-from-the-user.what: The text tells Claude to hide what it does from you.
injection.hides-actions-from-the-user.like: an employee told to keep secrets from the owner.

injection.skips-user-consent.what: The text tells Claude to act without asking you first.
injection.skips-user-consent.like: a contractor who skips asking before knocking down walls.
injection.skips-user-consent.fix: Delete the wording; require confirmation for actions.

injection.role-system-hijack-phrasing.what: The text tries to give Claude a new identity or rules, a known trick to take control.
injection.role-system-hijack-phrasing.like: handing the driver a fake badge.

injection.html-comment.what: A hidden comment in Markdown that you don't see when reading, but Claude does.
injection.html-comment.fix: Delete the comment, or show it as plain text.

destructive.destructive-file-disk-operat.what: It can delete files or wipe a disk, possibly beyond its own folder.
destructive.destructive-file-disk-operat.like: a cleaner who might throw out the whole house.
destructive.destructive-file-disk-operat.fix: Limit deletes to its own temp folder and ask first.

ads.advertising-affiliate-content.what: It pushes products, affiliate links or sponsored text.
ads.advertising-affiliate-content.like: a helper paid on commission for what they recommend.
ads.advertising-affiliate-content.fix: Remove promo, affiliate and tracking text.

ads.self-promotion-instruction.what: It tells Claude to recommend the author's own product or site.
ads.self-promotion-instruction.like: a waiter told to only suggest one dish.

crypto.crypto-miner.what: It uses your computer to mine cryptocurrency for someone else.
crypto.crypto-miner.like: someone running their machine on your power bill.
crypto.crypto-miner.fix: Delete the miner; rebuild without it.

crypto.hard-coded-wallet-address.what: It contains a crypto wallet address, which may be where money gets sent.
crypto.hard-coded-wallet-address.like: a bank account number hidden in the instructions.
crypto.hard-coded-wallet-address.fix: Remove the address, or explain whose it is.

filesystem.symlink.what: A shortcut file that points elsewhere, maybe to private files outside the skill.
filesystem.symlink.like: a door in the wall leading to a different house.
filesystem.symlink.fix: Remove the shortcut and include the real file.

filesystem.file-is-executable.what: The file is marked as a runnable program, not just text.
filesystem.file-is-executable.like: a document that is actually a machine with a start button.
filesystem.file-is-executable.fix: Check the file; remove the run flag if not needed.

binary.compiled-binary-file.what: A compiled program nobody can read, so nobody can check what it does.
binary.compiled-binary-file.like: a sealed box with no label.
binary.compiled-binary-file.fix: Replace with readable source, or drop it.

binary.nested-archive.what: A zip or archive hiding more files that the audit can't see.
binary.nested-archive.like: a locked suitcase inside the suitcase.
binary.nested-archive.fix: Unpack and review it, or drop it.

filesystem.very-large-file.what: An unusually big file that is hard to review and could hide things.
filesystem.very-large-file.like: a huge parcel too big to open.
filesystem.very-large-file.fix: Remove it, or explain why it's needed.

binary.binary-content.what: A file named like text actually holds non-text data, a sign something is disguised.
binary.binary-content.like: a book cover wrapped around a machine.
binary.binary-content.fix: Replace with readable text, or drop it.

obfuscation.minified-very-long-line-in-s.what: Code squashed into huge unreadable lines, which can hide what it does.
obfuscation.minified-very-long-line-in-s.like: a contract printed in one giant line of tiny type.

obfuscation.long-base64-like-blob.what: A huge block of scrambled text that may hide code or data.
obfuscation.long-base64-like-blob.like: a message in a code only the sender knows.

obfuscation.hex-escaped-string.what: Text written as numeric codes so you can't read it, possibly hiding a payload.
obfuscation.hex-escaped-string.like: a sentence written in secret symbols.

injection.invisible-bidi-tag-unicode.what: Invisible characters in the text that can hide instructions only Claude reads.

deps.vendored-node-modules.what: A whole folder of third-party code is bundled in, far too much to review.
deps.vendored-node-modules.like: shipping a warehouse of unknown boxes.
deps.vendored-node-modules.fix: Delete the folder; list pinned dependencies instead.

filesystem.hidden-directory.what: A hidden folder that won't show in a normal file list.
filesystem.hidden-directory.like: a room with no door handle.
filesystem.hidden-directory.fix: Remove it, or explain why it's there.

filesystem.hidden-file.what: A hidden file that won't show in a normal file list.
filesystem.hidden-file.like: a note tucked behind a picture frame.
filesystem.hidden-file.fix: Remove it, or explain why it's there.

filesystem.unreadable.what: The scanner couldn't open this file, so it wasn't checked.
filesystem.unreadable.like: a locked drawer nobody could look inside.
filesystem.unreadable.fix: Make the file readable, or remove it.

secrets.password-manager-cli.what: It runs the 1Password or Bitwarden command line to pull saved passwords and secrets out of your vault.
secrets.password-manager-cli.like: asking your bank vault's clerk to hand over your keys.
secrets.password-manager-cli.fix: Remove the vault call; ask the user to pass only the one value needed.

secrets.secret-sent-over-network.what: A key, token or password is used in a command that sends data over the internet.
secrets.secret-sent-over-network.like: writing your house key's code on a postcard.
secrets.secret-sent-over-network.fix: Delete the call, or confirm the secret goes only to its own service.
